ce:2006:q1.question:
Solution for the system defined by the set of equations
4y + 3z = 8;
2x - z = 2 and
3x + 2y = 5 is

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Linear Algebra
detailed_solution.markdown:
The augmented matrix for given system is,

$$\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 0 & 4 & 3\\ 2 & 0 & -1\\ 3 & 2 & 0 \end{matrix}\right|\begin{matrix} 8\\ 2\\ 5 \end{matrix} \right ]\xrightarrow[]{exchange 1st and 2nd row}\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 2 &0 & -1\\ 0 & 4 & 3\\ 3 & 2 & 0 \end{matrix}\right|\begin{matrix} 2\\ 8\\ 5 \end{matrix} \right ]$$

then by Gauss elimination procedure

$$\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 2 & 0 & -1\\ 0 & 4 & 3\\ 3 & 2 & 0 \end{matrix}\right|\begin{matrix} 2\\ 8\\ 5 \end{matrix} \right ]\xrightarrow[]{R_{3}-\frac{3}{2}R_{1}}\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 2 &0 & -1\\ 0 & 4 & 3\\ 0 & 2 & 3/2 \end{matrix}\right|\begin{matrix} 2\\ 8\\ 2 \end{matrix} \right ]\xrightarrow[]{R_{3}-\frac{2}{4}R_{2}}\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 2 & 0 & -1\\ 0 & 4 & 3\\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{matrix}\right|\begin{matrix} 8\\ 8\\ -2 \end{matrix} \right ]$$

For last row we see 0=-2 which is inconsistent

$\therefore$ Solution is non-existent for above system.

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2006:q2.title: GATE CE 2006 | Set 1 | Question: 2
ce:2006:q2.question:
The differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}=0.25y^2$ is to be solved using the backward
(implicit) Euler's method with the boundary condition y=1 at x=0 and with
 a step size of 1. What would be the value of y at x=1 ?

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Ordinary Differential Equation
detailed_solution.markdown:
$\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}=0.25y^{2} \;\;\left ( y=1\: at\: x=0 \right )$

$h=1$

Iterative equation for backward (implicit) Euler methods for above equation would be,

$\frac{y_{k+1}-y_{k}}{h}=0.25y^{2}_{k+1}$

$\Rightarrow \;\; y_{k+1}-y_{k}=0.25h y^{2}_{k+1}$

$\Rightarrow \;\; 0.25h y^{2}_{k+1}-y_{k+1}+y_{k}=0$

putting k=0 in above equation

$0.25h y^{2}_{1}-y_{1}+y_{0}=0$

since $y_{0}=1$ and $h=1$

$0.25 y_{1}^{2}-y_{1}+1=0$

$y_{1}=2$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ce:2006:q23.title: GATE CE 2006 | Set 1 | Question: 23
ce:2006:q23.question:
A class of first year B. Tech. students is composed of four batches A, B, C and

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Probability and Statistics

Let the mean and standard deviation of the students of batch C be $\mu _{c}$ and $\sigma _{c}$ respectively, and the mean and standard deviation of entire class of first year students be m and s respectively.

Now given,

$$\begin{aligned}   \mu _{c}&=6.6 \\     \sigma _{c}&=2.3\\   \mu &=5.5 \\     \sigma &=4.2 \end{aligned}$$

In order to normalise batch C to entire class, the normalised score must be equated.

since

$$\begin{aligned}   Z&=\frac{x-\mu }{\sigma } \\     Z_{c}&=\frac{x_{c}-\mu _{c}}{\sigma _{c}}=\frac{8.5-6.6}{2.3}\\ \text{Now  } Z&=\frac{x-\mu }{\sigma }=\frac{x-5.5}{4.2} \end{aligned}$$

Equating these two and solving, we get,

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{8.5-6.6}{2.3}&=\frac{x-5.5}{4.2} \\ \Rightarrow \;\;  x&=8.969\simeq 9.0 \end{aligned}$$

ce:2006:q24.title: GATE CE 2006 | Set 1 | Question: 24
ce:2006:q24.question:
A $2^{nd}$ degree polynomial, f(x) has values of 1, 4 and 15 at x = 0, 1 and 2, respectively. The integral $\int_{0}^{2}f(x)dx$ is to be estimated by applying the trapezoidal rule to this data. What is the error (defined as "true value - approximate value")
in the estimate ?

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Probability and Statistics
detailed_solution.markdown:
f(x)=1, 4, 15 at x=0, 1 and 2 respectively

$\int_{0}^{2}f\left ( x \right )dx =\frac{h}{2}\left ( f_{1}+2f_{2}+f_{3} \right )$(3 point Trapezoidal Rule)

Here  h=1

$\therefore \;\; \int_{0}^{2}f\left ( x \right )dx=\left ( 1+2\times +15 \right )=12$

$\therefore$ Approximate value by Trapezoidal Rule =12

Since f(x) is second degree polynomial, let,

$$\begin{aligned}  f\left ( x \right )&=a_{0}+a_{1}x+a_{2}x^{2} \\      f\left ( 0 \right )&=1 \\ \Rightarrow  \;\; a_{0}+0+0&=1 \\ \Rightarrow   \;\;   a_{0}&=1 \\      f\left ( 1 \right )&=4 \\ \Rightarrow \;\;  a_{0}+a_{1}+a_{2}&=4 \\ \Rightarrow  \;\; 1+a_{1}+a_{2}&=4 \\ \Rightarrow \;\;   a_{1}+a_{2}&=3 \;\;\;...(i)\\      f\left ( 2 \right )&=15 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; a_{0}+2a_{1}+4a_{2}&=15 \\ \Rightarrow \;\;1+2a_{1}+4a_{2}&=15 \\ \Rightarrow   \;\; 2a_{1}+4a_{2}&=14 \;\;\; ...(ii) \end{aligned}$$

Solving (i) and (ii) $a_{1}=-1$ and $a_{2}=4$,

$\therefore  \;\; f\left ( x \right )=1-x+4x^{2}$

Now, exact value of

$$\begin{aligned} &\int_{0}^{2}f\left ( x \right )dx \\   &=\int_{0}^{2}\left ( 1-x+4x^{2} \right ) \\   &=\left [ x-\frac{x^{2}}{2}+\frac{4x^{3}}{3} \right ]_{0}^{2}=\frac{32}{3} \end{aligned}$$

Error = Exact-Approximate value

$=\frac{32}{3}-12=-\frac{4}{3}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2006:q26.title: GATE CE 2006 | Set 1 | Question: 26
ce:2006:q26.question:
Using Cauchy's integral theorem, the value of the integral (integration being
taken in counterclockwise direction) $\oint_{c}\frac{z^{3}-6}{3z-i}dz$ is

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Calculus
detailed_solution.markdown:
Cauchy's integral theorem is,

$$\begin{aligned} f\left ( a \right )&=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{c}\, \frac{f\left ( z \right )}{z-a}dz\\ \text{i.e., } \oint_{C}\, \frac{f\left ( z \right )}{z-a}dz&=2\pi i\, f\left ( a \right ) \\ \text{Now, } \oint_{C}\, \frac{z^{3}-6}{3z-i}dz&=\frac{1}{3}\oint_{c}\, \frac{z^{3-6}}{\left ( z-\frac{i}{3} \right )} \end{aligned}$$

Applying Cauchy's integral theorem,

$$\begin{aligned}  &=\frac{1}{3}\left ( 2\pi i\: f\left ( \frac{i}{3} \right ) \right ) \\   &=\frac{1}{3}\left ( 2\pi i\left [ \left ( \frac{i}{3} \right )^{3}-6 \right ] \right ) \\   &=\frac{1}{3}\left [ 2\pi i\left ( \frac{i^{3}}{27}-6 \right ) \right ] \\ &=\frac{2\pi }{81}i^{4}-4\pi i \\   &=\frac{2\pi }{81}-4\pi i \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2006:q29.title: GATE CE 2006 | Set 1 | Question: 29
ce:2006:q29.question: The solution of the differential equation, $x^{2} \frac{dy}{dx}+ 2xy - x + 1 = 0$ , given that at x = 1, y = 0 is

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Ordinary Differential Equation
detailed_solution.markdown:
Giiven, $x^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+2xy-x+1=0 \;\; \left ( x=1, y=0 \right )$

$x^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+2xy =x-1$

Dividing by $x^{2}$,

$\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+\left ( \frac{2}{x} \right )y =\left ( \frac{x-1}{x^{2}} \right )$

which is a linear first order differential equation of the form,

$\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+Py =Q$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Integrating factor}&=I.F=e^{\int Pdx}=e^{\int \frac{2}{x}dx} \\     &=e^{2\log x} \\     &=e^{\log_{e}x^{2}}=x^{2} \\   y\times I.F&=\int Q\left ( I.F \right )dx \\    y.x^{2}&=\int \left ( \frac{x-1}{x^{2}} \right ).x^{2}.dx \\     &=\int \left ( x-1 \right )dx \\    yx^{2}&=\frac{x^{2}}{2}-x+C \\ \text{Now at }x=1, \;y=0,\\ \text{i.e. }   0\times 1^{2}&=\frac{1^{2}}{2}-1+C \\     0&=\frac{1}{2}-1+C \\     C&=\frac{1}{2} \\ \therefore \;\;  yx^{2}&=\frac{x^{2}}{2}-x+\frac{1}{2} \\   y&=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{2x^{2}} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2006:q52.title: GATE CE 2006 | Set 1 | Question: 52

and the consumptive use is 15 mm/d. If the irrigation efficiency is 60%, what
should be the frequency of irrigation such that the moisture content does not fall
below 50% of the maximum available moisture ?

detailed_solution.concept: Irrigation Engineering - Crop Water Requirements
detailed_solution.markdown:
Depth of maximum available moisture,

$d_{w}=\frac{\gamma d}{\gamma_{w}}(F-\phi)$

Field capacity

$$\begin{aligned} &= \frac{\text { weight of water retained by soil }}{\text { weight of same area of soil }} \\ &=\frac{\gamma_{w} \times V_{v}}{\gamma \times V} \\ \text { But } \frac{V_{v}}{V}&=n \\ \therefore \text { Field capacity } &=\frac{\gamma_{w}}{\gamma} \times n\\ \Rightarrow \frac{\gamma_{\mathrm{w}}}{\gamma} &=\frac{n}{\text{Field capicity}} \\ \Rightarrow \frac{\gamma_{\mathrm{w}}}{\gamma} &=\frac{0.45}{0.38} \\ \therefore \quad \quad d_{w} &=\frac{0.45}{0.38} \times 1 \times[0.38-0.1] \\ &=0.331 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

But the moisture content should not fall below 50 %

$\therefore$ Depth of water required

$=0.5 \times 0.331=0.165 \mathrm{m}$

Actual depth stored

$=\frac{0.165 \times 60}{100}=0.099 \mathrm{m}=99 \mathrm{mm}$

Frequency of irrigation

$$\begin{array}{l} =\frac{\text { Actual depth stored }}{\text { Consumptive use }}=\frac{99}{15} \\ =6.63 \mathrm{d} \simeq 6 \mathrm{d} \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

Jam density,

For maximum traffic volume,$\frac{d q}{d k}=0$

$$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad U_{s f}\left(1-\frac{2 k}{k_{j}}\right)&=0 &\left[\because U_{sf}\neq 0 \right ]\\ \Rightarrow \quad 1-\frac{2 k}{k_{j}}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad k&=\frac{k_{j}}{2} \end{aligned}$$

detailed_solution.markdown: The effect of increase in certain rapid sand filter and influent particle characteristics on time ($T_{B}$) for reaching particle breakthrough (turbidity $\gt$ 2.5 NTU) in the effluent, and time ($T_{H}$) of reaching terminal head-loss($\gt$ 3 m) across filter bed are given below. Effect of increase in filter depth (L) $T_{B}$ : $T_{B}$ will increase since particles in water will have the opportunity to potentially interact with more collectors, and hence the change for particle attachment to a collector is more. $T_{H}$: Since bed depth is more, water is encounter more resistance is passing through the bed. Hence $T_{H}$ will decrease. Effect of increase in superdicial velocity ($V_{s}$) $T_{B}$: Since pore velocity is more, the shear forces experianced by collected particles will be more. Hence particle detachment will be more, leading to a decrease in $T_{B}$. $T_{H}$: Since particle loading rate on the filter and rate of particle collection in the filter will increase, the porosity of the filter bed will decrease more rapidly, leading to more rapid head-loss buildup and hence a decrease in $T_{H}$. Effect of increase in floc strength $T_{B}$: Particle detachment due to shear force will become less prominent leading to increase in $T_{B}$. $T_{H}$: Since particle retention in the filter will be more, the porosity of the filter bed will decline faster leading to faster buildup of head-loss and hence $T_{H}$ will decrease. Effect of non-addition of coagulant $T_{B}$: If no coagulants are added, the particles will be stable and hence will not attach efficiently to the filter media. Hence $T_{B}$ will decrease. $T_{H}$: Since rate of particle clollection in the filter media will be lower as described above, the rate of head-loss buildup will also be lower, leading to an increase in $T_{H}$. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

detailed_solution.markdown: In strain diagram, $$\begin{aligned} \frac{O E}{O A}&=\frac{0.002}{0.0025} \\ \Rightarrow \quad O E&=\frac{4}{5} x_{u} \\ \Rightarrow \quad O E&=0.8 x_{u} \\ \therefore A E&=x_{u}-0.8 x_{u}=0.2 x_{u} \end{aligned}$$ $\therefore \quad$ Total compressive force, $$\begin{aligned} &= 0.45 t_{c k} \times 0.2 x_{u} \times b+\frac{2}{3} \\ & \times 0.45 f_{c k} \times 0.8 x_{u} \times b \\ &= 0.33 f_{c k} b x_{u} \end{aligned}$$ Actual NA depth, $$\begin{aligned} C&=T\\ \Rightarrow \quad 0.33 f_{c k} b x_{u}&=0.87 f_{y} A_{s t} \\ \Rightarrow \quad x_{u}&=\frac{0.87 \times 250 \times 1500}{0.33 \times 30 \times 250}=131.8 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}$$ $\therefore$ Total compressive force, $$\begin{aligned} &=0.33 \times 30 \times 250 \times 131.8 \\ &=326 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2006:q80.title: GATE CE 2006 | Set 1 | Question: 80
